source.citation: 'Bird’s-Eye View of Old Fort Dearborn.' Illustration at p. 27 of J. Seymour Currey, The Story of Old Fort Dearborn (Chicago: A. C. McClurg & Co., 1912). Numbered reconstruction of the first fort, not a contemporary view.
what_it_does_not_supply: An eyewitness, independent testimony from 1803–1812, or a dated record of when the upper walks or blockhouse lanterns were built.
Any dimension, coordinate, bearing, measured roof slope, gallery depth, post section, rail height, baluster spacing or floor thickness.

Independent identification of every existing named range’s interior facade: the near faces are concealed, and the reconstruction’s main entrance and magazine arrangement must not displace Whistler’s contemporary measured plan.
Colour, material tone, or agreement between all pictorial reconstructions.
what_it_supplies: Two-storey courtyard gallery treatment on the visible inner barracks/quarters ranges: an upper walk with close vertical rail pales over the open lower level, under a roof near the main eave.
The numbered caption identifies the main entrance (1), sally-port (2), western gateway (3), NW and SE blockhouses (4,5), officers quarters (6), barracks (7), and magazine (8).
The roofed blockhouse lanterns as a retrospective representation, without a construction date.
